slots.practicalActivity: In a sandbox or Developer Edition org, open Setup and search "data import" and "data loader" to see both entry points, then open System Overview and note the current data storage percentage and API requests used in the last 24 hours; walk through the seven-item planning checklist for a hypothetical 50,000-row Lead import.
slots.deliverable: A completed planning checklist (object/volume, source/quality, duplicates, required fields, tool choice, limits, backup) for a hypothetical Lead import, plus the actual System Overview storage/API numbers from your org.

slots.practicalActivity: Launch the Data Import Wizard against Leads with a small CSV (5-10 rows), deliberately leave one column unmapped to see how the wizard flags it, then map it and finish the import; check the Bulk Data Load Job page afterward for the success file.
slots.deliverable: A completed Data Import Wizard job with a downloaded success file, plus a short note describing what the "Unmapped" flag looked like before you fixed it.

slots.practicalActivity: Download and install Data Loader (requires JRE 17+) in your own environment, open it to see the six-button main screen, and locate the Settings dialog to check Batch size and Server host before running anything for real.
slots.deliverable: A working local Data Loader install, confirmed by opening the six-operation main window and locating the Settings dialog (Batch size, Server host) without having run a job yet.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a 5-row CSV for fake Lead records with at least one company name containing a comma (properly quoted) and one date field in yyyy-MM-dd format; save it as CSV UTF-8, then open the raw file in a plain text editor to confirm the comma-containing value is correctly quoted.
slots.deliverable: A clean, pre-flight-checked CSV file (header row, consistent dates, quoted commas, UTF-8 encoding) ready to load, with the raw text editor view confirming correct quoting.

slots.practicalActivity: In a sandbox, export 10 Account records and note their 18-character IDs; build a CSV updating one field for 5 of those records using the real IDs and run Update to confirm only those 5 changed, then add 2 new rows with blank ID cells and run Upsert matched on Id, confirming the 5 existing rows update again while the 2 new ones insert.
slots.deliverable: Two completed Data Loader jobs (one Update, one Upsert) with their success files, showing the Update affecting exactly 5 existing records and the Upsert correctly updating 5 and inserting 2 new ones.

lessons.title: External IDs and Relationships During Loads

slots.practicalActivity: Create a custom text field on Account called Legacy_Customer_Number__c, mark it External ID and Unique; upsert a small Account CSV matched on that field, then build a Contacts CSV using Account.Legacy_Customer_Number__c dot notation and confirm each Contact lands under the correct Account without looking up a single Salesforce ID by hand.
slots.deliverable: A Unique External ID field on Account, an upserted batch of Accounts matched on it, and a batch of Contacts correctly linked to their parent Accounts via dot-notation relationship mapping.

slots.practicalActivity: Run a full upsert lab end to end: create Legacy_Contact_ID__c as a Unique External ID on Contact, build a 10-row Contact CSV, upsert it and confirm 10 successes with Created=true, then change two rows' Email values and re-run the upsert, confirming those two now show Created=false.
slots.deliverable: Two Data Loader success files from the same CSV run twice — the first showing 10 inserts, the second showing 2 updates and 8 unchanged matches — proving upsert idempotency.

slots.practicalActivity: Without referring back to the lessons, write out the planning checklist, the three operations (Insert/Update/Upsert) and their matching behavior, and the External ID dot-notation pattern from memory; then check your notes against a real field mapping screen in Data Loader or the Import Wizard.
slots.deliverable: A one-page "Getting Data In" cheat sheet (planning checklist + operation comparison table + External ID pattern) written from memory and verified against the live tool.

lessons.title: Data Exports and Backups
lessons.chapterTitle: Getting Data Out and Keeping It Safe

slots.practicalActivity: In a sandbox, navigate to Setup's Data Export page, click Export Now, deselect "Include all data" and choose just Account and Contact, leave attachments unchecked, and start the export; once complete, download the files and open the Contact CSV to find the AccountId column.
slots.deliverable: A completed manual data export (Account + Contact only) with both CSV files downloaded, and the AccountId column identified as the "flattened" relationship reference.

lessons.title: Weekly Export Service
lessons.chapterTitle: Getting Data Out and Keeping It Safe

slots.practicalActivity: On the same Data Export page, click Schedule Export and walk through the configuration screen, setting a frequency (weekly if your edition allows it, otherwise monthly) and start date; note which frequency your edition actually offers.
slots.deliverable: A configured (or reviewed, if not left active) scheduled export with a documented frequency setting and a note on whether your edition supports weekly vs. monthly.

lessons.title: Bulk Data Operations
lessons.chapterTitle: Getting Data Out and Keeping It Safe

slots.practicalActivity: In Data Loader's Settings, check "Use Bulk API," run a small Update job and confirm it completes, then reopen Settings and uncheck it to confirm "Insert null values" reappears as an option; separately, run a job that explicitly nulls a field using the literal #N/A value in a CSV cell.
slots.deliverable: One Data Loader job run successfully with Bulk API enabled, plus a documented test showing a field explicitly cleared to null using #N/A (not a blank cell) under Bulk API.

lessons.title: Deleting and Mass Transferring Records
lessons.chapterTitle: Getting Data Out and Keeping It Safe

slots.practicalActivity: In Setup, open Mass Transfer Records, choose Transfer Accounts, set a Transfer from and Transfer to user, search with criteria, and review the matched list and relationship checkboxes (without clicking the final transfer button); separately, open Mass Delete Records for a test object, build search criteria, and run a delete with "Permanently delete" left unchecked so results land in the Recycle Bin.
slots.deliverable: A reviewed Mass Transfer Accounts screen (criteria + relationship checkboxes documented) and a completed non-permanent Mass Delete, with deleted records confirmed sitting in the Recycle Bin.

lessons.title: Recycle Bin and Data Recovery
lessons.chapterTitle: Getting Data Out and Keeping It Safe

slots.practicalActivity: Delete a test record, then use the App Launcher to find the Recycle Bin and Restore it; toggle between My Recycle Bin and Org Recycle Bin to see the difference in what's listed, and check the Deleted Date column against the 15-day retention window.
slots.deliverable: A successfully restored test record from the Recycle Bin, with notes on the difference between My and Org Recycle Bin views and the 15-day retention countdown observed.

slots.practicalActivity: Design a backup-and-recovery plan combining this chapter's tools: a scheduled export frequency, a rule for when to use Mass Delete with "Permanently delete" checked vs. unchecked, and a note on the Recycle Bin's 15-day limit as the reason scheduled exports matter as a second layer.
slots.deliverable: A one-page written backup/recovery policy referencing the scheduled export cadence, the Mass Delete permanent-delete decision rule, and the Recycle Bin's 15-day limit.

slots.practicalActivity: In Setup, open All Duplicate Rules and All Matching Rules, activate the standard Account matching rule and duplicate rule (both start inactive), set its Action On Create to Block with custom Alert Text, then attempt to create a duplicate test Account and confirm the save is blocked with your alert text shown.
slots.deliverable: An activated standard Account duplicate rule (Block action, custom alert text) with a note confirming a duplicate-Account save attempt was actually blocked.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a custom Matching Rule on Contact combining an Exact match on Email with a Fuzzy match on Name (AND'd together), wire it into a new Duplicate Rule with Allow+Report action, then test it against two Contacts that are fuzzy-name matches but have different emails to confirm it does NOT flag them, since Email must also match.
slots.deliverable: A custom Matching Rule (Exact Email AND Fuzzy Name) referenced by a new Duplicate Rule with Allow+Report, tested against both a true match and a near-match that correctly doesn't trigger it.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a validation rule on a custom or standard object requiring a specific field whenever another field reaches a particular value (using the AND/ISPICKVAL/ISBLANK pattern), with a user-facing error message pinned to the relevant field; test it by attempting a save that should be blocked and one that should pass.
slots.deliverable: An active validation rule with a formula using AND/ISBLANK/ISPICKVAL, tested with one blocked save and one successful save demonstrating the rule only fires on the intended condition.

slots.practicalActivity: Enable State and Country/Territory Picklists in a sandbox (or review the setting if already enabled) and note how an existing free-text State value is handled during the cleanup pass; separately, build a before-save record-triggered Flow on a custom text field that applies TRIM and UPPER (or PROPER) to normalize every save.
slots.deliverable: A before-save Flow that normalizes one free-text field on every save, verified by saving a record with inconsistent casing/whitespace and confirming it's cleaned automatically.

slots.practicalActivity: Take the lesson's 5-row messy CSV (or build an equivalent one with case, spacing, and punctuation inconsistencies), clean it in a spreadsheet using TRIM/PROPER/SUBSTITUTE formulas in helper columns, and identify which cleaned rows are now identical (likely duplicates) versus which still need a human decision (e.g., a blank email).
slots.deliverable: A cleaned CSV with a documented helper-column formula pass, flagging which rows became identical duplicates and which still have unresolved completeness gaps.

slots.practicalActivity: Write your own five-item pre-import checklist (field mapping, completeness, picklist exactness, test batch, duplicate-rule action) and apply it to a real test import of 15-20 rows in your sandbox, running the small test batch first before considering a larger file.
slots.deliverable: A completed five-item pre-import checklist applied to an actual 15-20 row test batch import, with the import's success/error results documented against each checklist item.

slots.practicalActivity: Combine the chapter's tools on one object: active duplicate + matching rules, one validation rule, one before-save standardization Flow, and a picklist conversion — then run a deliberately messy test batch through the whole stack and document which layer caught which problem.
slots.deliverable: One object configured with all four data-quality layers active simultaneously, tested with a messy batch, and a table mapping each caught problem to the specific layer that caught it.

slots.practicalActivity: Review your layered-defense results against the "picklists -> validation rules -> matching/duplicate rules -> before-save Flow -> periodic review" order, identify any layer that let something through it should have caught, then adjust that layer's configuration.
slots.deliverable: A short written retrospective naming one gap found in the layered defense and the specific configuration change made to close it.

slots.practicalActivity: Run the full lesson lab: create Legacy_Contact_ID__c as an External ID on Contact, build a 10-row Contact CSV, upsert it and confirm 10 successes with Created=true in the output file, then change two rows' emails and re-run to confirm those two show Created=false.
slots.deliverable: Two Data Loader success files from running the same upsert file twice, demonstrating correct insert-then-update behavior with Created=true/false columns as evidence.

slots.practicalActivity: Deliberately break an import in three ways (a missing required field, a lookup pointing at a non-existent External ID, and a value exceeding a field's length) and run it; sort the resulting error file by the Error column, fix the dominant cause first, and re-import only the previously-failed rows until the error file is empty.
slots.deliverable: An error file worked down from multiple error types to zero, with a written log naming each error code encountered (REQUIRED_FIELD_MISSING, INVALID_CROSS_REFERENCE_KEY, STRING_TOO_LONG, etc.) and its specific fix.

slots.practicalActivity: Replicate the Meridian Outdoor Supply migration at small scale: combine two small CSVs representing two "regions" with overlapping company names and inconsistent state/phone formatting, load Accounts first with upsert on an External ID, confirm success, then load Contacts referencing those Accounts, and review the duplicate-rule report for likely cross-region duplicates.
slots.deliverable: A small multi-region migration completed in the correct sequence (Accounts before Contacts), with a documented duplicate-rule report flagging cross-source near-duplicates for manual review.

slots.practicalActivity: Build one end-to-end data-management pipeline in a Developer org: plan a load, prepare and clean a CSV, upsert it with a Unique External ID, export a backup before and after, and work any resulting error file down to zero — documenting every step.
slots.deliverable: A complete, documented end-to-end data load (plan -> clean -> upsert -> backup -> error resolution) run successfully in a Developer org, ready to describe in a job interview.

monthlyMilestoneContribution: After this course, a student can plan and execute real Salesforce data loads with the Import Wizard and Data Loader (insert/update/upsert, External IDs, Bulk API), safely export and recover data, and build a layered data-quality defense — duplicate rules, validation rules, and standardization — to keep an org's data clean at scale.
